Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3346; unchangeable, or (neuter as abstract) unchangeability:--immutable(-ility).
BiblicalUsage: Unchangeable, and Hebrews uses it for the two things God cannot do. God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath, that by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation. The word is the counsel that cannot be moved, and the oath that cannot be broken.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for unchangeable carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the consolation, that the heirs of promise have two things that cannot move, and that is why they can hold on.
